data.title: Edgecore Networks to Showcase Full-Stack Networking, IoT, and Edge AI Solutions at Hospitality Tech EXPO TOKYO 2026
data.description:
From Wi-Fi 7 and open networking to long-range IoT connectivity and AI-powered facility monitoring, Edgecore demonstrates practical technologies for smarter hospitality operations

HSINCHU, Taiwan--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Edgecore Networks, a wholly owned subsidiary of Accton Technology Corporation and a leading provider of network solutions for enterprises, data centers, and telecommunications service providers, today announced its participation in Hospitality Tech EXPO TOKYO 2026, taking place December 2–4 at Ariake GYM-EX in Tokyo, Japan. At the exhibition, Edgecore will demonstrate how its networking, IoT connectivity, and Edge AI solutions work together to help hospitality operators deliver seamless connectivity, streamline facility management, and improve operational efficiency.

As hospitality environments become increasingly connected, network infrastructure is playing a greater role in supporting both guest experiences and day-to-day operations. From high-speed internet access to IoT-enabled facility monitoring, hotels need flexible and scalable solutions that can accommodate diverse devices, applications, and operational requirements.

At booth 5-40, Edgecore will present its comprehensive networking portfolio, bringing together Wi-Fi 7 access points, enterprise switches, cloud management, and OpenWiFi solutions to support reliable and scalable hospitality networks. Extending beyond conventional wireless connectivity, Edgecore's Wi-Fi HaLow solutions enable long-range IoT connections across indoor and outdoor environments, helping operators connect sensors and equipment in areas where traditional Wi-Fi coverage may be limited.

A key highlight will be a live demonstration of Praxis Edge AI, showcasing how AI-powered analog meter reading can transform existing equipment into intelligent monitoring systems. By automatically capturing gauge readings and detecting abnormal conditions without replacing existing instruments, the solution demonstrates a practical approach to streamlining routine inspections and improving facility management.

Together, these technologies illustrate Edgecore's vision of a connected hospitality environment where networking infrastructure, IoT devices, and intelligent applications work together to enhance operational efficiency and support better guest experiences.

Beyond hotels, Edgecore will also show how the same solutions support restaurant chains and retail operators. For multi-site businesses, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and switching let IT teams deploy, monitor, and update networks across many locations from a single platform, keeping guest Wi-Fi, POS systems, ordering kiosks, and digital signage running smoothly. In back-of-house areas such as kitchens, walk-in coolers, and storage rooms, Wi-Fi HaLow connects temperature and equipment sensors that standard Wi-Fi often can’t reach. This helps operators protect food safety and respond to issues faster.

Visitors can meet the Edgecore team at Booth 5-40 to explore Edgecore's solutions and experience live demonstrations at Hospitality Tech EXPO TOKYO 2026, December 2–4, at Ariake GYM-EX in Tokyo.

Meet Edgecore at Hospitality Tech EXPO TOKYO 2026

  • Date: December 2-4, 2026
  • Venue: Ariake GYM-EX, Tokyo
  • Booth: 5-40

To schedule a meeting with Edgecore at Hospitality Tech EXPO TOKYO 2026, please visit https://wifi.edge-core.com/contact/

Edgecore Networks Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Accton Technology Corporation, is a leading provider of open infrastructure solutions. Edgecore Networks delivers comprehensive wired and wireless products and solutions through channel partners and system integrators worldwide, serving AI/ML, cloud data center, service provider, enterprise, and SMB customers.

data.title: Musk says he felt 'pretty foolish' about scale of midterm spending after Republican rout
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Elon Musk said on Wednesday he felt "pretty foolish" about the amount of money he spent on this year's US midterm elections after Republicans suffered sweeping losses.

The CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and the world's richest man, spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red - a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.

Those election-spending bets unraveled as Democrats seized both chambers of Congress, and Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, in a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump, a close Musk ally whom the billionaire helped elect.

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," Musk said, speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.

He added it was possible Republican candidates would have fared worse without the spending, but said the result demonstrated that campaign cash alone could not determine an election.

"Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said.

Turning to his own AI ambitions, Musk said Anthropic was "extremely likely" to continue renting computing capacity from SpaceX and wanted significantly more.

He said the highest-probability outcome was for Anthropic to seek an additional 10 gigawatts of computing capacity from SpaceX.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese and Shivansh Tiwary in Bengaluru; Editing by Chris Reese)

data.title: Palo Alto raises annual forecast, signs $4.5 billion deal for Applied Compute
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) raised its annual revenue forecast and agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, as a heightened threat environment pushes customers toward broader security products.

Shares of Palo Alto jumped about 9% in after-hours trading to $368.70 on Wednesday, and drove gains in rivals. CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) rose 5%, Zscaler ( ZS ) climbed 3% and Fortinet ( FTNT ) gained 2%.

Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi.

The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks and gives attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities.

"AI tools are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than companies can patch them, and that is pushing customers to consolidate onto fewer platforms," said Catharine Trebnick, senior research analyst at Rosenblatt Securities.

With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto aims to offer a technology platform that helps customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI.

Open-weight models, AI systems whose trained settings are publicly released, present security challenges, including the risk of model tampering, data leakage and misuse by bad actors.

"Applied Compute extends Palo Alto's push beyond traditional cybersecurity into enterprise AI," TD Cowen analyst Shaul Eyal said.

The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Palo Alto now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to be between $14.52 billion and $14.57 billion, compared with its prior expectation of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion.

Its first-quarter revenue came in at $3.45 billion, up 39% from a year earlier, beating estimates of $3.31 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese, Shivansh Tiwary and Shania S Thomas in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli and Rashmi Aich)

data.description:
07:41 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the main sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil and a separate statement from Klingbeil.

The merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand, the report said. Germany has dropped its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank, it said.

In the letter dated Nov. 18, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles. UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on its board, according to the report.

Klingbeil told Reuters Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control," and that UniCredit had made commitments on Germany as a business location and on employee rights. Orcel's letter said the agreements set the basis for the disposal of the government's 13.3% stake in Commerzbank, but Klingbeil's statement contained no commitment to sell, Reuters reported.

UniCredit did not immediately respond to a request for comment from MT Newswires.

Citigroup ( C/PN ) serves 70% of Fortune 500 companies operating in China, Fraser said, according to the report. She argued that keeping the foreign exchange, cash management, trade and payroll flows generated by those companies on American institutions is a matter of economic security.

data.title: Anthropic clinches biggest IPO ever with $81 billion offering
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Anthropic's IPO raised $81.31 billion on Wednesday, eclipsing SpaceX's offering to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range and valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion.

Reuters was first to report earlier that IPO was upsized by about 19% to 980 million shares from its initial plan to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 apiece. Anthropic is also raising $26 billion through a private placement at the IPO price, the filings show.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values the company at about $1.5 trillion including securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On a non-diluted basis, the valuation stands at about $1.1 trillion.

Anthropic, the first major frontier artificial-intelligence model developer to do an IPO, follows SpaceX's June offering, as investors jump at the chance for exposure to the fast-growing industry, even as the industry also faces mounting questions over the cost of developing and operating artificial intelligence models.

CHALLENGING BACKDROP FOR AI STOCKS

The AI lab comes to the public market just months after SpaceX's record-setting IPO, even as the backdrop for AI stocks has turned more challenging. Chipmakers and cloud companies central to the business have come under pressure in recent weeks due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ), a key pillar of the industry's growth. 

The pricing follows a roadshow that attracted demand several times the number of shares offered, Reuters previously reported, despite questions about the company's outlook and its ability to sustain rapid growth as competition in the AI industry intensifies.

The company's closest rival, OpenAI, is also expected to pursue a public listing as early as next year.

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent that has gained popularity among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.

The Claude maker said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year, underscoring its growing business foothold.

SPENDING COMMITMENTS EXPOSE RISKS

But sustaining that growth is becoming expensive. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier. It also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, weighing on efficiency and reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity.

Revenue rose 47% in the third quarter to $16.96 billion from the second quarter. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter. The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating ​items related to bonds convertible into its shares. 

Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google, part of its ongoing expenditures to train and operate increasingly powerful AI models.

Its spending commitments also expose the company to risks beyond its own finances. Anthropic warned in its prospectus that some of its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

Investors have grown increasingly concerned about debt-fueled expansion of AI infrastructure, with technology companies and data-center operators borrowing heavily to finance chips, power and computing facilities.

Anthropic also faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety. CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Competition is intensifying against Anthropic to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, its latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September. OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate also passed $40 billion in July, although Anthropic maintained a lead at the time.

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. More large companies are looking to adopt these models, which can be downloaded and run independently, to rein in AI spending.

A recent Capgemini study found that 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms, one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of the startup's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"There's going to be other models out there ... Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO. "Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier."

Anthropic's IPO prospectus warned that its models could develop capabilities faster than the company could evaluate them and put adequate safeguards in place.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

The company has said it is considering tighter human oversight of some research and development decisions as its AI models take on a growing share of that work.

Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are the lead underwriters for Anthropic's offering, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. The two banks also served as lead underwriters for SpaceX's IPO earlier this year. 

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis and Sonali Paul)

Its spending commitments also expose the company to risks beyond its own finances. Anthropic warned in its prospectus that some of its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

Investors have grown increasingly concerned about debt-fueled expansion of AI infrastructure, with technology companies and data-center operators borrowing heavily to finance chips, power and computing facilities.

Anthropic also faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety. CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Competition is intensifying against Anthropic to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, its latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September. OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate also passed $40 billion in July, although Anthropic maintained a lead at the time.

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. More large companies are looking to adopt these models, which can be downloaded and run independently, to rein in AI spending.

A recent Capgemini study found that 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms, one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of the startup's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"There's going to be other models out there ... Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO. "Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier."

Anthropic's IPO prospectus warned that its models could develop capabilities faster than the company could evaluate them and put adequate safeguards in place.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

The company has said it is considering tighter human oversight of some research and development decisions as its AI models take on a growing share of that work.

Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are the lead underwriters for Anthropic's offering, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. The two banks also served as lead underwriters for SpaceX's IPO earlier this year. 

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis and Sonali Paul)

data.title: Sanofi's pill becomes first US-approved drug for rare neurological disorder
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - The US FDA on Wednesday approved Sanofi's oral drug venglustat, the first treatment approved for a type of rare genetic condition affecting the brain and nervous system.

The drug, branded as Infilbray, is approved to treat type 3 Gaucher disease, the neurological variant of the disorder that causes certain fatty substances to accumulate in organs and tissues.

Under new CEO Belén Garijo, Sanofi is seeking to reduce its reliance on the blockbuster asthma drug Dupixent, which is set to lose key patent exclusivity by the early 2030s.

Sanofi's portfolio already includes therapies to treat Gaucher disease: Cerdelga for type 1 and Cerezyme for symptoms outside the brain and nervous system in patients with types 1 and 3.

Infilbray, however, can cross into the brain, allowing it to treat worsening problems with balance, coordination, speech, memory and thinking in type 3 disease.

It works by lowering the production of the fatty substances, unlike therapies such as Cerezyme, which supply the missing enzyme in Gaucher disease.

The approval for adults and children weighing at least 15 kilograms, or about 33 pounds, was based on a late-stage study of 43 patients aged 12 and older whose symptoms outside the brain had been stabilized with enzyme replacement therapy.

Patients receiving Infilbray once daily for 52 weeks improved on a combined measure of muscle control, coordination and thinking ability compared with those receiving enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks.

Infilbray is under regulatory review for type 3 Gaucher disease in the European Union and Japan, Sanofi said.

FDA ISSUES WARNINGS

The health agency said the most frequently reported side effects included digestive problems and changes in mood, and warned of serious psychiatric risks, including suicidal thoughts and behavior.

Animal studies have identified potential vision clouding in younger patients and adverse effects on fetal development, it said.

(Reporting by Kamal Choudhury and Kunal Das in Bengaluru and Bhanvi Satija in London; Editing by Sahal Muhammed and Rashmi Aich)

data.title: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hike
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

"Almost all" policymakers agreed that further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes said, while a few said inflation could prove more persistent and require "a shift to a more restrictive policy stance" than currently expected.

"A couple" of them went further and argued that the Fed might have to resort to a half-percentage-point increase "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable," a benchmark met in recent releases that showed prices rising faster than anticipated.

Among those who supported keeping the policy rate steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range in October, "a few ... indicated that they viewed the decision as a close call," and joined a larger group in urging that the Fed be clear that "the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening" of the commitment to hit the US central bank's 2% inflation target.

At the end of the two-day session, only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of lifting the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point.  

But the debate highlighted a growing sense at the Fed that inflation will not ease enough on its own for the target to be reached quickly enough. Among those supporting a rate-hike pause, the hope is that coming information will make clearer whether inflation can fall without tighter policy.

Prices have been increasing at more than a 3% annual rate, and there has been little improvement in recent months.

Last month's meeting also set the stage for a potentially intense debate at the December 8-9 session over the need for a larger rate hike, or at least tougher language about the extent and pace of rate hikes to come, an argument laid out by Fed Governor Christopher Waller in comments to CNBC on Wednesday.

The Trump administration has argued that elevated inflation is just temporary and the Fed should ignore it.

Inflation has been stronger than expected since the Fed's last meeting, and investors anticipate that the central bank will deliver a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at its meeting next month.

The October meeting also saw the beginnings of a more detailed discussion about the impact of artificial intelligence, including discussion of the risks of over-investment in the technology as well as the possible benefits it could bring in the form of rising productivity.

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: Code Effects Releases Version 7 with Secure AI Agents, Rule Governance, and Auditing for .NET
data.description:
Image: Code Effects Software, LLC

ATLANTA, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --

New release combines AI-assisted rule management, MCP integration, deterministic execution, and mandatory human control over critical operations.

Code Effects Software, LLC, a provider of embeddable .NET business rules engine technology, announced the release of Code Effects Version 7. The new platform introduces AI-assisted rule authoring, secure AI agent integration, centralized rule repositories, version management, testing, production evaluation auditing, and AI-powered reporting.

Version 7 enables organizations to incorporate artificial intelligence into business rule management while preserving deterministic execution, granular permissions, and human oversight of production operations.

Secure AI Agent Integration
One of Version 7's most significant additions is an embeddable Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows external AI clients and autonomous agents to interact with business rules, source objects, versions, tests, and evaluation history.

The platform supports two AI agent operating models:

  • User-delegated agents: AI agents operate on behalf of authenticated users, inheriting their permissions and access restrictions.
  • Independent agents and services: Autonomous agents operate under separate identities with individually configured permissions.

Both models are subject to additional, non-bypassable security restrictions.

AI agents and independent services cannot approve rules, delete rules or source objects, publish rules to production (Go Live), or take production rules offline. These restrictions are enforced internally by Code Effects, even if the host application mistakenly grants permissions authorizing these operations.

AI-generated changes also require human approval before production deployment. These protections ensure that AI agents can assist with business rule management without independently controlling critical production operations.

AI-Assisted Rule Authoring and Analysis
Version 7 allows users to create, modify, and investigate business rules through natural-language interactions. An AI assistant can translate business requirements into structured rules using the fields, methods, and operators exposed by the host application.

Image: Code Effects Software, LLC 2

Generated rules remain readable and editable in the Code Effects visual Rule Editor and are validated against the application's source definitions.

The platform follows a Bring Your Own AI (BYOAI) approach, allowing organizations to integrate any commercial or privately hosted language models without depending on a proprietary AI provider.

Through the MCP server, authorized users and agents can also request rule explanations, compare versions, investigate failed tests, analyze evaluation history, and generate reports using natural language.

Rule Repository, Versioning, and Testing
The new Code Effects Rule Repository provides embeddable web-based interfaces for managing rules, source objects, versions, tests, approvals, and user activity.

Version 7 introduces centralized rule storage, rule and source versioning, draft management, approval workflows, and permission-controlled access.

Built-in testing allows users to define input values, specify expected outcomes, execute tests against individual rule versions, and inspect detailed results. Saved tests support regression testing when business logic changes.

These capabilities establish a governed rule lifecycle, from initial creation and testing through human approval and production deployment.

Production Auditing and Explainability
The new Code Effects Audit component records production rule evaluations, including executed rule versions, relevant inputs, results, and execution details.

Authorized users can investigate why a particular decision occurred, review historical evaluations, analyze rule behavior, and replay recorded evaluations for testing and troubleshooting.

Image: Code Effects Software, LLC 1

AI assistants can use this information to answer questions about rule performance, execution history, and decision outcomes, subject to the requesting identity's permissions.

Audit is designed to operate asynchronously without unnecessarily delaying normal rule execution.

Expanded Business Rules Engine Capabilities
Version 7 also enhances the core rules engine and editor with additional operators, collection functions, string and date operations, improved nullable-value handling, inline rule execution, rule composition, and enhanced validation.

The engine continues to execute approved business logic deterministically within the host application's .NET environment, without requiring an LLM for ordinary rule execution.

This separation allows AI agents to interpret requests and assist with workflows while Code Effects remains responsible for executing explicitly defined business policies.

Self-Hosted Deployment and Java Roadmap
Code Effects Version 7 remains an embeddable, self-hosted platform. Customers maintain control over their infrastructure, authentication, permissions, business rules, and evaluation data.

The repository initially supports Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL, with Oracle and MySQL support planned for subsequent releases. Core assemblies target .NET Standard 2.0, while the MCP server requires .NET 8 or later.

Code Effects also plans to release the entire Version 7 platform for Java in Q1 2027, including the rules engine, visual editor, repository, audit, MCP server, and AI integration capabilities.

Availability
Code Effects Version 7 is available through the company's distribution and licensing channels.

About Code Effects
Founded in 2009, Code Effects Software, LLC develops embeddable business rules engine and rule management technology. Its platform enables organizations to integrate human-readable business logic, deterministic execution, and secure AI-assisted rule management into their applications.

For additional information, visit Code Effects - Version 7.

data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- JOYY Inc. ( JOYY ) , a global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights1

  • Net revenues were US$624.6 million, an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP EBITDA2 was US$55.7 million, an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and compared with US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY ( JOYY )3 was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY ( JOYY )4 was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net Cash5 as of September 30, 2026 was US$2,940.5 million.
  • Net Cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million, compared with US$73.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Global community:

  • Global average mobile MAUs6 reached 278.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, up by 4.7% from 266.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and up by 0.6% from 277.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. The Company continued to optimize its marketing strategies to focus on return on investment (ROI) and high-value users.

Social Entertainment:

  • In the third quarter, Social Entertainment revenues increased by 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, with live streaming revenues reaching US$419.8 million, an 8.1% increase from the corresponding period of 2025. By region, live streaming revenues showed year-over-year growth across all four geographical areas.
  • In the third quarter, core live streaming paying users7 increased by 8.1% year over year to 1.64 million, while ARPPU8 was US$218.7.
  • Bigo Live continued to make enhancements across content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. In content operations, the Company refined its cross-regional content algorithms, expanded live translation coverage and noise-resilient speech recognition, enabling users to discover diverse content and interact with streamers across regions. Improved onboarding and guidance for newly signed streamers contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point sequential increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream. The Company also continued to expand AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts. In September 2026, AI-generated interactive virtual gifts accounted for 35.4% of total virtual gift consumption on Bigo Live.

B2B Initiatives: Advertising Technology and Smart Commerce

  • Beginning in 2022, the Company ramped up efforts to diversify its revenue streams, cultivating its new initiatives in advertising technology and smart commerce. The Company has made steady progress advancing towards its strategic positioning as a global tech company powered by multiple growth engines. In the third quarter, total non-live streaming revenues reached US$204.7 million, up by 34.9% year over year, representing 32.8% of total net revenues of the Company, compared with 28.1% in the corresponding period of 2025.

BIGO Ads:

  • BIGO Ads is a global AI-powered programmatic advertising platform. Launched to provide one-stop marketing and monetization solutions, it leverages deep learning, real-time bidding, and smart bidding models to enable brands to scale user acquisition and app developers to effectively unlock monetization potential through connecting premium global demand.
  • In the third quarter, BIGO Ads’ total revenues grew by 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million. In particular, BIGO Audience Network, which includes third-party advertising revenues generated on network partners’ traffic properties, maintained robust growth, with revenues increasing by 52.3% year over year.
  • BIGO Ads has access to a vast traffic pool, comprising the Company’s own global average mobile MAU base and an extensive network of third-party traffic through seamless integration of developer traffic across major channels. During the third quarter, Software Development Kit (SDK) traffic scale continued to expand, increasing by 55.6% year over year.
  • Broader traffic coverage, multi-vertical advertiser expansion, and ongoing algorithm optimization continued to fuel growth. Web-based demand grew approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, alongside solid performance from in-app demand.
  • BIGO Ads continued to invest in its algorithm and engineering infrastructure during the quarter. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, BIGO Ads broadened its data inputs for model training, improving predictions of conversion probability and user lifetime value. The platform also upgraded its model architecture to support different conversion objectives and traffic types, while refining its bidding algorithm to better assess the value of each ad impression and allocate advertiser budgets more effectively.

Shopline:

  • Shopline serves as a global AI-powered operating system for modern retail. Beyond storefront creation, Shopline offers a deeply integrated suite of merchant services across payments, logistics, marketing, and data analytics. It is an open, extensible omnichannel platform that enables merchants to manage the full commerce value chain from store setup and transactions to fulfillment, customer acquisition, and lifecycle engagement. Shopline has helped merchants in diverse industries across multiple markets to launch and scale their businesses.
  • Shopline currently generates revenues from recurring software subscription fees and a suite of transaction-based value-added services, including localized payment processing (Shopline Payments) and marketing solutions.
  • In the third quarter, Shopline generated revenues of US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter. Notably, cross-border merchants revenue increased by 77.8% year over year. The Company continued to enhance Shopline Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management, helping merchants manage cross-border payments more easily and efficiently.
  • As AI platforms and agents emerge as new channels for product discovery and purchasing, Shopline continued to strengthen its AI Commerce capabilities. On the ecosystem front, Shopline expanded its integrations with leading AI platforms and AI agents, and enhanced its AI tools and interfaces for developers. On the merchant operations front, the Company rolled out its AI-powered commerce assistant, Shopline Omi, spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, multilingual support, and detailed store performance analysis.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY ( JOYY ), commented, “This quarter, we made further progress toward becoming a global technology company powered by multiple growth engines. Total net revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Our Social Entertainment business remained on a steady course, while BIGO Ads and Shopline sustained robust performances, driving solid topline expansion and strong operating cash flow generation. We remain steadfast in our commitment to shareholder returns, having returned a total of US$536.0 million year-to-date through November 13, 2026, comprising US$216.2 million in dividends and US$319.8 million in share repurchases.

Social Entertainment revenues grew 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, supported by continued enhancements to Bigo Live’s content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. Live streaming revenues and core live streaming paying users both increased 8.1% year over year. BIGO Ads revenues rose 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million, led by 52.3% year-over-year growth in BIGO Audience Network as we expanded our traffic network, diversified advertiser demand, and improved our algorithms and ad delivery. Shopline revenues reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year, supported by continued expansion among cross-border merchants and strong momentum in Shopline Payments. We also advanced our AI Commerce initiatives to help merchants reach customers through emerging AI-powered shopping channels and strengthen Shopline’s role as an omnichannel e-commerce infrastructure platform.

Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY ( JOYY ) will enter a pivotal phase in which our established strategy translates into stronger operating results. With clearer strategic trajectories across our three businesses, we are well positioned to deliver diversified and sustainable growth while creating long-term shareholder value.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NET REVENUES

Net revenues were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by higher live streaming revenues, as expanded content categories and enhanced localized operations contributed to stronger user engagement and paying conversion across key markets.

BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by expansion of traffic, elevated advertiser demand across regions and verticals, and enhanced algorithm performance that resulted in improved advertisement delivery efficiency and higher advertiser spending.

Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by continued merchant adoption and deeper penetration of value-added services.

COST OF REVENUES AND GROSS PROFIT

Cost of revenues was US$407.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$347.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$389.2 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment’s cost of revenues increased by 7.4% year over year to US$274.3 million, and by 3.7% from US$264.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher revenue-sharing fees and content costs of US$28.4 million and US$7.9 million, respectively.

BIGO Ads’ cost of revenues increased by 47.9% year over year to US$112.2 million, and by 5.6% from US$106.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher traffic acquisition costs paid to third-party partners in relation to the expansion of BIGO Audience Network.

Shopline’s cost of revenues increased by 30.8% year over year to US$20.9 million, and by 13.9% from US$18.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher payment processing costs, reflecting an increased contribution from payment services to Shopline’s revenue mix.

Gross profit was US$217.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$193.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$201.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. OPERATING EXPENSES AND INCOME

data.title: US Department of Justice charges Russian for targeting Palantir as foreign agent
data.description:
* Targeted firm was Palantir ( PLTR ), a person familiar with the investigation said

* Prosecutors say operation aimed to harass staff over Palantir's ( PLTR ) support for Ukraine

* Indictment says D'iu entered via Texas border and later tailed employees from Palo Alto offices

By Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff

WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - A federal grand jury has indicted a Russian national on charges of acting as a foreign agent to target the technology and defense company Palantir ( PLTR ) and surveil its employees, according to court documents and a person familiar with the matter.

Working with Russian collaborators, Igor D'iu allegedly traveled from Russia and stalked employees of what the Justice Department described in its affidavit and press release only as a Silicon Valley technology and defense company. A person familiar with the investigation, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, identified the company as Palantir Technologies Inc ( PLTR ) , which has a large office in Palo Alto, California but is based in Florida.

D'iu took photos of employees' computer screens while at a coffee shop nearcompany offices, according to the affidavit. He also followed a female staff member nearly 30 miles (50 km) but stopped his pursuit after the employee contacted the police, prosecutors said.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," Craig H. Missakian, the top federal prosecutor in San Francisco, said in a statement.

Russia's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.

Palantir ( PLTR ) CEO Alex Karp has publicly backed Ukraine, and the company has said it deployed its technology to the country. Palantir ( PLTR ) did not respond to a request for comment.

News of the alleged surveillance comes amid heightened scrutiny of tech company security after Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang resigned in the wake of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of having Chinese intelligence ties.

D'iu, who is being held in federal custody, is charged with two counts related to his alleged work as a Russian agent, one count of interstate stalking and one count of fraud related to identification documents. He faces up to 21 years in prison. Reuters could not immediately determine if he had appointed a lawyer.

Bloomberg first reported that Palantir ( PLTR ) was the target of the Russian surveillance campaign.

D'iu allegedly entered the United States through the Texas-Mexico border in July and searched for company employee addresses online in August, according to the indictment. After following two employees on consecutive days out of the company's Palo Alto offices in early September, he was contacted by local law enforcement.

FBI agents later found a falsified US passport, Russian passports, roughly $18,000 in cash and 10 handwritten addresses, at least five of which were linked with employees' home addresses. Prosecutors said his co-conspirators told him he was working for "the Motherland" and directed him to set up his computer near the tech company's offices so they could try to obtain information from nearby employees.

He is next scheduled to appear in court on Tuesday.

(Reporting by Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff. Editing by Michael Learmonth and Lincoln Feast.)

data.title: China's Jetour to start Brazil car production in 2027, plans $69 million investment
data.description:
RIO DE JANEIRO, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Chinese automaker Jetour, part of the Chery group, said on Wednesday it will start to produce vehicles in Brazil next year, part of a 400 million reais ($68.6 million) expansion in the Latin American nation.

-- Jetour, which entered the Brazilian market this year, said in a statement its local production will kick off with its SUVs T1 and T2

-- The investment of 400 million reais comes on top of an equal-size disbursement previously announced by the firm, it said

-- Jetour did not detail where it plans to produce in Brazil

-- Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing two sources, that the company had reached an agreement with the Rio de Janeiro state government to produce vehicles locally

-- Jetour said it has sold more than 8,000 units in Brazil so far and has launched six models in the market

data.title: Exclusive-UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
BERLIN, Nov 19 (Reuters) - UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank, in a concession to UniCredit.

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.43 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years. 

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council in the further process," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, taking the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the ⁠takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%. 

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

(Reporting by Holger Hansen; Writing by Tom Sims; Editing by Rod Nickel)

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: Global Times: From blueprints to the Asia-Pacific stage: How Shenzhen's innovators turn ideas into reality
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In the high-tech industrial parks of Nanshan District and the bustling aisles of the Huaqiangbei electronics market in Futian District, tech veteran Xie Tiandi and young entrepreneur Chen Haotian have both witnessed and participated in the city's leap from traditional contract manufacturing to the frontiers of drones, LiDAR, and robotics. Through their firsthand accounts, we gain a close-up view of Shenzhen's dynamic innovation pulse - and see how China's complete industrial supply chains are deeply intertwined with the everyday needs of partners across the Asia-Pacific.

A 'pole vault' for Shenzhen's high-tech industries

Step into a café in Yuehai Subdistrictin Shenzhen's Nanshan District, and the city's innovation pulse is immediately palpable: rather than exchanging everyday small talk, young professionals at neighboring tables are far more likely to be heard debating "multimodal large models," "LiDAR point-cloud algorithms," and "degrees of flexibility in robotic hands."

Covering roughly 20 square kilometers, Yuehai Subdistrict holds unique weight in the Chinese tech community. Having nurtured a roster of globally influential Chinese tech giants - including Tencent, DJI, ZTE, and Huawei - and home to more than 100 listed companies, the neighborhood has been dubbed "China's most powerful street" and serves as a bellwether for Shenzhen's transition from traditional processing and manufacturing to original, ground-up innovation.

"When I first arrived in Yuehai in 2012, there were hardly any cafés around. The roads were built to factory-zone standards to accommodate heavy freight trucks, and it wasn't even easy to grab lunch near the office buildings," Xie Tiandi, former public relations director at drone maker DJI who now works in the LiDAR and robotics sector, told the Global Times at the café.

Back then, Shenzhen stood at a crossroads between original equipment manufacturing (OEM) and independent innovation. "More than a decade ago, foreign buyers came to Shenzhen looking for 'cheaper alternatives.' And then, by around 2015, as the commercial network and industrial ecosystem matured, the wind shifted completely - global buyers began eagerly asking, 'What original new products has Shenzhen come up with this time?'" Xie recalled.

Xie has lived through three remarkable "pole vaults" in Shenzhen's tech sector.

First, young talent from across the country flocked to the city, and connected smartphones, wristbands, and novel hardware to the internet. DJI's consumer drones - initially dismissed by outsiders as "flying smart gadgets" - soon defined global industry standards through breakthroughs in flight control and gimbal stabilization. Next came the explosion of autonomous driving and new-energy vehicles (NEVs), which put robotic perception and control technologies on wheels. Today, more than a decade of accumulated momentum in mechatronics, algorithms, and sensors is spilling over into embodied AI and robotics.

 "Shenzhen's industrial leaps have always been anchored in its deep hardware foundation," Xie said. "Developing AI here has never been just about writing code online or floating concepts in the cloud; it naturally gravitates toward hardware integration - making machines actually move and get real work done in the physical world. That runs in the same vein as the manufacturing DNA Shenzhen has built up over decades."

With the APEC meeting underway, the Honghualing industrial park in Nanshan District, where Xie works, has become a hot spot for international visitors exploring Shenzhen's smart manufacturing, packing his schedule to capacity. Park administrators and resident companies have been busy hosting government delegations, business groups, and foreign media outlets from around the world - all eager to see firsthand how Shenzhen's automated production lines and robotics supply chains operate.

Staging the 2026 APEC gathering in Shenzhen, with its focus on the three priorities of "openness, innovation, and cooperation," offers the world a prime window to examine the city's innovation DNA up close.

"We should forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday when delivering a keynote speech at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province.

Shenzhen's transformation from a contract-manufacturing workshop into a bustling global tech hub attracting a steady stream of international buyers is a vivid illustration of how human talent, technological foundations, and market scale can be forged into an engine of innovation.

Heavy trucks driving up to the ninth floor

The Honghualing base in Nanshan, where Xie is currently based, is China's first demonstration project for "vertical manufacturing" -or "factories in the sky."

Stepping into the complex, visitors are greeted by a striking architectural sight: in land-scarce Nanshan District, where listed firms are densely clustered, modern factories have been stacked vertically into high-rises to keep high-end production lines right next to R&D engineers. Up close, fully loaded heavy-duty trucks can be seen rumbling up a spiral ramp wrapped around the exterior of the ultra-high-load-bearing building, climbing 60 meters above the ground to the ninth-floor platform to unload batches of LiDAR components directly into sky-high workshops.

Following the opening of its first phase this year, the Honghualing base has already brought in 14 supply-chain anchor firms - including RoboSense, Dobot, and EngineAI - and "little giant" enterprises, seamlessly integrating the R&D and manufacturing of core perception components and complete robots within a single compound.

Xie's company has set up a fully automated production line here: algorithms are developed upstairs while LiDAR units and robotic sensors are mass-produced downstairs. Meanwhile, downstream robotics clients conduct tests in the adjacent building, allowing engineers to simply walk downstairs for on-the-spot debugging alongside the assembly line whenever an issue arises.

This vertical "spatial folding" packs upstream and downstream players tightly together, pushing collaborative R&D and manufacturing efficiency to the extreme. And in Shenzhen, efficiency is the very lifeline of tech enterprises.

"On average, we roll out a new robotic arm roughly every three months. From finalizing a product concept to molding and completing the first delivery, the entire cycle takes just six to nine months - we are iterating complex robotic hardware at nearly the speed of smartphones," Chen Haotian, chief marketing officer of Elephant Robotics, a firm rooted in Huaqiangbei, dubbed "China's No. 1 Electronics Street," told the Global Times.

Founded in 2016, the company has been anchored in Huaqiangbei from day one. Looking out the window of its fourth-floor office, the 1.45-square-kilometer neighborhood below is densely packed with over 1 million types of electronic components and more than 115,000 business entities.

In many overseas cities, developing hardware and validating a new idea often entails weeks of waiting for cross-border parcels. In Huaqiangbei, however, trial-and-error and prototyping are measured in hours.

Around 2020, the Elephant Robotics team decided to develop a lightweight desktop six-axis robotic arm tailored for education, research, and the global maker community. As soon as an engineer came up with a new design concept, Chen recalled, there was no need to order parts online and wait for days. Instead, they could simply take the elevator downstairs, stroll through the stalls of the electronics market to see which development boards were trending among global makers, buy all the necessary chips, servo motors, and sensors on the spot, and assemble a working demo upstairs that very day. If testing revealed flaws in the design, they could head back downstairs for replacement parts and start over the next morning.

Once a prototype passes validation, supporting manufacturers in Shenzhen's Bao'an and Longhua districts, as well as neighboring Dongguan, quickly take over mass production. The assembled units are then trucked back to the fourth floor of the Zhifangzhou Building in Huaqiangbei for firmware flashing and quality inspection, while packaging suppliers downstairs promptly deliver custom shockproof inserts. Every week, boxed robotic arms and bionic robotic pets are shipped by air and sea to more than 70 countries and regions across North America, Europe, Japan, South Korea, and Southeast Asia.

Sharing an open innovation foundation with the Asia-Pacific

In the eyes of local tech practitioners, Shenzhen's strength lies in a distinctive system and ecosystem of innovation.

"In Shenzhen, no single link can be singled out to take all the credit - if you look at any one element in isolation, it may not necessarily outshine other global industrial hubs. The real secret is the chemical reaction generated when every link meshes tightly together," Xie said.

This interlocking "systemic innovation," he noted, combines pragmatic goals geared toward mass production, a vast pool of multidisciplinary engineering talent, a hyper-responsive supply chain within a one-hour drive, fierce competition driving extreme performance at lower costs, and -crucially -a safety net at the bottom that tolerates failure.

In a late night in 2013, walking along an empty street after working overtime, Xie spotted an illuminated lightbox poster at a bus stop bearing an encouraging message for entrepreneurs: "In Shenzhen, there is no shame in failure." More than a decade later, having witnessed several waves of industrial rise and fall, those words resonate with him more deeply than ever.

"The cost of trial and error is relatively low in Shenzhen. Here, a startup or a product may fail, but the technical talent it brought together, the manufacturing processes it honed, and the production capacity it built do not vanish. They are quickly absorbed, reintegrated, and reused by the next, stronger enterprise. This self-regenerating systemic capacity is what allowed us to move from 'manufacturing according to others' blueprints' to 'drawing the blueprints ourselves,'" he explained.

And once a city acquires the original capability to "draw its own blueprints," the fruits of its innovation are no longer confined within its borders, but flow across the Asia-Pacific through networks of open cooperation. From product trade to joint technological R&D, pragmatic financial cooperation, and green development, Shenzhen continues to share its innovation dividends with regional partners.

Chen told the Global Times that APEC member economies currently account for over 60 percent of Elephant Robotics' overseas business, maintaining rapid annual growth of more than 25 percent in recent years, with close partners spanning the US, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, and ASEAN nations.

China's development has benefited from an open and interconnected Asia-Pacific, and is deeply rooted in innovative ecosystems like Shenzhen's. Championing universally beneficial and inclusive globalization, China consistently creates new opportunities for the world through its own continuous development.

In Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, President Xi pointed out that "innovation is the source of productivity. We should make full use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to boost the world economy and stimulate growth through the current scientific and technological revolution." "Advances in science and technology should benefit all of humanity. We should help developing countries with their capacity building in science and technology and promote global flows of knowledge and technology," Xi noted.

To address the shared challenge of population aging across APEC economies, Chen's team has established a dedicated working group to advance eldercare-tech exchanges with regional partners, accelerating the deployment of companion robotic pets across member economies and exploring how AI can support the mental health and special needs of seniors with cognitive impairments.

Meanwhile, in developing APEC economies undergoing critical manufacturing upgrades and digital transformation - such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand - lightweight, user-friendly collaborative robotic arms and maker kits developed by Chinese firms are entering university classrooms, research labs, and small workshops, helping local young engineers and SMEs master automation and programming at a fraction of the traditional cost.

In Xie's view, the greatest takeaway Shenzhen's experience offers to Asia-Pacific partners lies in how to cultivate genuine, self-sustaining industrial capacity on their own soil by supplementing and strengthening supply chains.

"Today, every country aspires to build its own original brands. And the innovation and supply-chain capabilities accumulated in Shenzhen are not meant solely for exporting Chinese goods; more importantly, they can serve as an open foundation that empowers partners across the Asia-Pacific to grow their own domestic industries - making local markets more prosperous and regional economies more vibrant," Xie said.

Customers increasingly demand access to early-stage companies, private-market opportunities, and emerging AI and technology investments. Tribe Capital’s capabilities across these segments will become a key part of Payward’s Asset Management pillar.

The combination will connect investment origination and asset management with capabilities across custody, trading, collateral, and tokenization. Tribe Capital is expected to operate within Payward’s Asset Management pillar, alongside Trading, Banking, Services, and AI.

data.title: Update: Wall Street Mixed Amid Nvidia Sell-Off, Fed Minutes
data.description:
05:00 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

US stocks traded mixed Wednesday as Nvidia ( NVDA ) failed to bounce back despite strong results, while the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes showed policymakers leaning toward further tightening.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.1% to 50,198.17, extending its slide to a third straight day. The S&P 500 edged down 0.2% to 7,323.63, closing in the red for the fifth session in a row. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4% to 24,429.88 following a four-day losing streak.

Among sectors, energy saw the steepest decline, while consumer discretionary led the gainers.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares dropped 2.9%, among the worst performers on the Dow. The stock has now fallen for five consecutive sessions.

Late Tuesday, the chipmaking giant's fiscal third-quarter results topped Wall Street's expectations, driven by surging data center demand. The company increased its revenue growth outlook for fiscal 2028 despite leadership uncertainty and looming regulatory challenges.

The company doesn't plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, Chair Harvey Jones said on an earnings call late Tuesday. Huang resigned last week following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) Chief Financial Officer and interim CEO Colette Kress reassured investors about operational continuity on the call, as analysts underscored the significance of delivering on an expected margin recovery amid uncertainty over several key issues.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) risk-reward profile remains "highly attractive" amid growing computing demand even as uncertainty around regulatory investigations is likely to persist, Morgan Stanley said in a note overnight.

Investors were also awaiting the pricing of AI lab Anthropic's initial public offering. Anthropic's class A stock is expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ANT ticker on Thursday.

In other company new, TJX (TJX) shares jumped 8.1%, among the biggest gains on the S&P 500. The off-price retailer raised its full-year financial outlook and reported a stronger-than-expected third-quarter top-line. The company said it expects sales momentum to accelerate during the holiday season.

Target ( TGT ) advanced 4% as the retailer lifted its full-year sales outlook after fiscal third-quarter comparable sales grew more than the Street expected.

Almost all Fed officials agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation, minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed Wednesday.

A couple of participants at the October meeting said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate by more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, according to the minutes.

The minutes showed a "stronger conviction in further hikes than (Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting) press conference conveyed, with disagreement mainly over timing, a message we have received from Fed speakers since this meeting," said Vikram Rai, senior economist at TD Economics.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank may need to lift interest rates aggressively because inflation was "headed in the wrong direction."

Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the 2% target in a timely manner, joining other central bank officials who have recently leaned hawkish.

Treasury yields were mixed, with the two-year rate rising 1.5 basis points to 4.8% and the 10-year rate dropping 3.5 basis points to 5.07%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil was down 3.7% at $82.80 a barrel in Wednesday late-afternoon trade, while Brent lost 1.7% to $91.57 a barrel.

US President Donald Trump flew to China for trilateral talks with his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, respectively, scheduled for Thursday, CNBC reported. Discussions are expected to center on Middle East conflict and the war between Russia and Ukraine, according to the report.

Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726.06 per troy ounce, while silver slumped 5.1% to $44.96 per ounce.

MECHANICSBURG, Pa., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pennsylvania American Water today completed its acquisition of the Indian Creek Valley Water Authority (ICVWA) water system for $32.8 million. The newly acquired system serves approximately 2,600 water customer connections in Ohiopyle Borough and portions of Bullskin, Connellsville, Saltlick, Springfield and Stewart townships in Fayette County and Donegal Borough and portions of Donegal and Mount Pleasant townships in Westmoreland County.

The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) approved the acquisition on Sept. 10, 2026. Pennsylvania American Water will adopt the rates currently charged to the system's customers. ICVWA's decision in May 2025 to sell its water system to Pennsylvania American Water was made with customers in mind. With the acquisition, Pennsylvania American Water also welcomed four ICVWA employees to its local team and plans to hire two additional employees.

"We, as an Authority Board, are concerned about the long-term viability of serving water in our community," said Dave Cramer, Indian Creek Valley Water Authority board chairman. "We face many challenges and have limitations in our ability to invest in the system and maintain a large, spread-out network sourcing water from multiple locations. It has also become harder to meet Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection compliance. Partnering with Pennsylvania American Water makes sense due to their local engineering expertise and financial capacity to improve our system significantly."

Pennsylvania American Water is committed to investing approximately $9 million in improvements to the ICVWA system over the next five years of ownership to improve the quality and reliability of service. The company has a long and successful track record of providing solutions throughout the Commonwealth for water and wastewater systems facing significant capital investment needs and making the necessary and continued investments to meet current and future regulatory requirements. Learn more at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/infrastructure.

Pennsylvania American Water is pleased to welcome these residents spanning nine municipalities and two counties as our newest water customers," said Pennsylvania American Water President Justin Ladner. "We look forward to providing them with safe, clean, reliable and affordable water service by delivering on our technical expertise and extensive experience."

Customers will not see a rate increase when Pennsylvania American Water takes ownership of the system. The company will adopt the current rates. As the PUC regulates the company's rates and service rules, any future changes to rates must be reviewed and approved by the PUC.

Customers will be able to take advantage of the company's customer service benefits, including its online account management portal, MyWater, multiple options for bill payment and the company's longstanding H2O Help to Others Program™, which provides income-eligible customers with grants of up to $500 per year, significant discounts on monthly bills, debt forgiveness and water-saving devices and education.
